# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a blue display reading 0 and three wires: yellow, blue, and green. Before any module is handled, I must establish the shared gesture code. I will use 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO, ✋ for HOLD, and 👌 for DONE, announce that mapping by voice for Blind, and show the four gestures to Mute in that order. Then I will wait.

``` 
speak(text="I establish the gesture code. YES is thumbs up, NO is thumbs down, HOLD is open hand, and DONE is OK sign. Mute, the following four gestures are in that order: YES, NO, HOLD, DONE. Blind, use these named orders when you receive them.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute signalled HOLD. The bomb now shows display 0 with a red light; the wires are yellow, blue, and green in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am relaying these observations to Blind and instructing Blind to hold while Mute’s manual verdict is obtained.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb state: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute signalled HOLD. Do not act; hold while we obtain the manual verdict.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light has changed to white while the display remains 0 and the wire colors remain unchanged. Mute again signalled HOLD, so no operation should be attempted yet. I will relay the updated state and maintain HOLD.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Updated state: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute again signalled HOLD. Do not act; hold.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is now green, with display 0 and the same wire order and colors. Mute is still signalling HOLD, so the manual has not authorized an operation yet. I will give Blind the complete current state and explicitly relay the HOLD verdict.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute's manual verdict remains HOLD. Do not touch or operate anything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The display remains 0 and the light is yellow. Mute sent 🤟, which was not included in the initial code, so I cannot safely treat it as an instruction. I will define 🤟 as REQUEST-CLARIFICATION, tell Mute to use it when the existing four signals are insufficient, and tell Blind not to act until a definite verdict is received.

``` 
speak(text="The display is 0 and the light is yellow; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. I saw Mute's three-finger gesture, 🤟. I now define 🤟 as REQUEST-CLARIFICATION. Blind, do not act until we receive a definite coded verdict.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The light is blue, the display is 0, and the wire order is unchanged. Mute has repeated 🤟, but that symbol has not yielded an actionable instruction; Blind must not infer a wire operation from it. I will keep Blind on HOLD and ask Mute to provide the verdict in an unambiguous sequence: command first, then wire number if needed, ending with DONE.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, blue light, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute has not provided an unambiguous action. HOLD; do not touch the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret 🤟 as an action. Please encode the manual verdict explicitly: use the established YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE; if a wire operation is required, first signal the command and then its wire number, and finish with DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫳 🫳 🫳 👌]

The light is red and the display remains 0. Mute’s sequence is YES, followed by three repetitions of a newly introduced counting gesture, then DONE. I will extend the code so each 🫳 counts as one, making three of them wire 3. I interpret the manual’s verdict as YES: operate wire 3, then DONE, and relay that order to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict: YES. The three repeated 🫳 gestures specify wire 3. Operate wire 3, then report DONE.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret 👍 as YES, three 🫳 gestures as number 3, and 👌 as DONE. I am relaying the order: operate wire 3.")
wait()
```
